**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• Construction zones: 35 mph unless otherwise posted. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• Yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights may only be used when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | TxDMV | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must use a tow bar or chain; cannot tow a vehicle that is not in motion.
• **Motorcycles**: Must wear a helmet; no seat belt.
• **Commercial Vehicles**: Additional regulations for size, weight, and driver qualifications. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 & TxDOT | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **TxDOT Website** – Regular updates on road conditions, speed limit changes, and construction projects. 2. **TxDMV** – For registration, insurance, and driver’s license information. 3. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text; available online through the Texas Legislature’s website. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances that may add to state law (e.g., city parking restrictions). --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted signs** – Texas has many “no parking” and “no stopping” zones that can be hard to spot. - **Use headlights** – Even on clear days, it’s safer to keep your lights on. - **Keep a safe following distance** – The “two‑second rule” is a good baseline. - **Avoid distractions** – Put your phone on “Do Not Disturb” while driving. - **Check weather alerts** – Texas can have sudden storms; adjust your driving accordingly. --- #### Need More Detail? If you’re looking for specifics on a particular law (e.g., “What are the penalties for a first‑time DUI?”) or want to know how a recent law change affects you, let me know! I can pull up the exact statutes or point you to the relevant TxDOT/TxDMV resources.
